Reconstructed as SetET4000Brightness(unsigned int level), static, finding 2. Writes the four-entry BW ramp through the DAC write-address and data ports 0x3C8/0x3C9, each entry scaled by level/64 and written three times. The multipliers are IOVGADisplayPrivate.h's WHITE_PALETTE_VALUE 63, LIGHT_GRAY_PALETTE_VALUE 48, DARK_GRAY_PALETTE_VALUE 30 and BLACK_PALETTE_VALUE 0, and the indices its WHITE_INDEX 3 through BLACK_INDEX 0. Two things the disassembly settles that the finding does not: the parameter is unsigned, because the divisions are plain shr (a signed int would need the round-toward-zero fixup) and -setBrightness:token: reaches this after an unsigned cmp 0x40 / jbe; and the scaled value is computed before the index is written, which is why the black entry materialises its zero into cl separately from the zero it writes as the index. Writing the value into a local before each index outb reproduces both. 240 bytes against the reference's 240 (237 of body plus three pad). Read against the full reference disassembly instruction by instruction, disassembled out of the Mach-O with capstone rather than taken from the finding's pseudocode, and our own build's body was disassembled and diffed back against it: the two instruction streams are identical, in the same order with the same registers and the same body length, the only textual difference being the absolute addresses of the __DATA operands, which differ because our __TEXT,__const is 170 bytes shorter (the build-generated _VGA_VERS_STRING / _VGA_VERS_NUM, already intentional-mismatch from Task 1).

Reconstructed as vga_write_bpp2packed32_to_bpp4planar(unsigned int *src, unsigned short *fb), external, finding 8. Masks each 16-bit half of the packed word with 0xAAAA (plane 1) or 0x5555 (plane 0), gathers the eight selected bits into a byte, complements it, and stores the two bytes as one 16-bit word; *src is re-read in each pass, which the reference's second load off edi shows. The writer's counts are -15,-12,-9,-6,-3,0,+3,+6 for plane 1 and one greater for plane 0, which is not finding 7's table minus one by any reading; the two functions are inverses, not offsets of one another. The disassembly is what was followed.
